thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — P1: cost-routing anomaly detected. Sudden spike in traffic routed to low-cost variant 'redwood/opt-quant-8bit-econ-v1' with downstream quality regressions. Auto-alert: quality-regression-rate > 8% over 10m on prod-global

maya (oncall): saw the alert, grabbing it. who's on call for routing policies? @arjun?

arjun (sre): on it. I'm pulling routing logs now. initial thought: a policy rollout changed cost-weighting across regions ~9m ago.

sam (ml-op): confirmed — recent policy flip (PR #4823) was meant to be canaryed but was applied globally. It increased cost-preference weight.

maya (oncall): customer-impact? any large customers affected?

emily (cs): AcmeCorp and Flowful on prod saw degraded summarization quality in last 15m, CS has 2 support tickets opened.

arjun (sre): metrics snapshot:
```
metric: routed_requests.variant
window: 10m
- stable-gen-2.1: 18%
- opt-quant-8bit-econ-v1: 72% (was ~5% baseline)
metric: quality_regressions.rate
window: 10m
- global: 8.9% (threshold 1%)
- eu-west: 12%
- us-west: 7%
```

sam (ml-op): here's the offending policy snippet from the deployment (redacted):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  name: economic-preference-v2
  rollout: GLOBAL
  parameters:
    prefer_cost: true
    cost_weight: 0.9  # intended 0.3 for canary, rolled out as 0.9
    quality_floor: 0.6
    fallback: allow_any_compatible_variant
```

maya (oncall): that cost_weight jump explains the spill. dumb mistake — can we fast rollback or override?

arjun (sre): propose immediate mitigation: override route weights for the affected route to pin to stable-gen-2.1 and disable economic-preference-v2. Two options:
1) Hot override via routing API (preferred, non-disruptive)
2) Revert policy deployment (slower)

sam (ml-op): I can push the hot override. command to set route weights:
```bash
# override weights for route: /v1/generate
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/routes/overrides" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","weights":{"redwood/stable-gen-2.1":0.95,"redwood/opt-quant-8bit-econ-v1":0.05},"reason":"temporary mitigation - spike to econ variant causing regressions"}'
```

maya (oncall): execute and confirm. emily, draft a short customer note: "We observed elevated error/quality regressions related to model routing; mitigation is in progress." keep it high level.

emily (cs): drafting. will message impacted customers individually after confirmation.

arjun (sre): override applied at 2065432120. seeing immediate shift in routing. verifying quality metrics...

incident-bot: Deploy bot: route override request accepted (id: override-2026-11-02-61).

arjun (sre): preliminary: opt-quant traffic down to 6% in 60s. quality_regressions.global down to 1.2% in 2m.

maya (oncall): great. keep monitoring for 30m. Sam, please run a quick sanity eval on a representative prompt set and paste examples here if anything still bad.

sam (ml-op): running quick eval on 25 prompts (summaries + code gen). sample failing case observed earlier:
INPUT: "Summarize the following meeting notes focusing on action items..."
RESP from opt-quant-8bit-econ-v1: "Key points: meeting went well. do the things." (missing actions)
RESP from stable-gen-2.1: "Action items: 1) Owner A to finalize PR by Thu; 2) Owner B to schedule follow-up meeting..."

maya (oncall): thanks. that's the kind of regression CS is seeing.

arjun (sre): root cause analysis so far: 1) policy change intended as canary was mis-deployed to GLOBAL due to CI/CD gating bug 2) the fallback logic 'allow_any_compatible_variant' combined with high cost_weight caused aggressive routing to cheaper quantized variant 3) no hard quality guard was triggered because quality_floor was too low for this workload (0.6).

emily (cs): any ETA on full rollback? customers asking for timeframe.

arjun (sre): immediate mitigation done via override. full rollback of policy PR and a follow-up revert will happen after we confirm stability (target: 30-45m).

sam (ml-op): follow-ups: add a canary-enforcement check in CI to prevent GLOBAL rollout unless canary metrics OK; increase quality_floor default; add per-route hard guard to block routing to variants with known eval regressions for that route type.

maya (oncall): actions/owners:
- arjun: monitor for 60m and rollback policy PR if no regression returns (done: override applied)
- sam: create PR for CI guard + quality_floor change (ETA 24h)
- emily: send customer note after 10m of stable metrics (ETA 15m)
- maya: incident doc + postmortem (ETA EOD)

arjun (sre): handoff: i'm going offline for a brief shift change at 2065432145. @maya, take ownership for monitoring for the next 30m; i'll be reachable if needed.

maya (oncall): taking over. we'll keep this P1 until metrics are stable for 30m.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Status update at 2065432160 — mitigation in place (route override), quality metrics trending back to baseline. Monitoring.

emily (cs): sending customer note now.

sam (ml-op): will capture example prompts + regressed responses for postmortem.

maya (oncall): next steps: postmortem to include timeline, root cause (canary gating bug), fix plan (CI guard, policy deployment safety, quality_floor increases), and customer follow-up template. Closing initial pager.

incident-bot: Incident record created: INC-2026-1102-0147. Severity: P1. Links: control-plane/INC-2026-1102-0147.

maya (oncall): thanks team. leaving notes in the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
